title: Umbilical hernia surgery
what: The surgeon puts the bulge back in place and closes the weak spot in the belly wall near the belly button. Often a mesh is placed to make it stronger.
why: For an umbilical hernia, especially if it grows, hurts, or bothers you. In adults it does not go away on its own.
duration: surgery usually takes 30 to 90 minutes; the hospital stay is usually from a few hours to 1 to 2 days
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. The doctor will tell you what to stop and when
Heart or lung disease, or diabetes
If you had belly surgery before
If you or your relatives ever had problems with anesthesia
If you smoke. It is best to quit ahead of time, so the wound heals better

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, an ECG, sometimes an ultrasound and a check-up with a general doctor. Your clinic will give you the list.

prepare.title: Pain relief
prepare.text: The anesthesiologist will offer general, spinal, or local anesthesia. The choice depends on the hernia size and your health.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food from the evening before, and no drinks for a few hours before. Your clinic will give you the exact time.

prepare.title: Things to bring
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes, slippers, a support belt if your surgeon prescribed one, and the medicines you take every day.

steps: On the day of surgery, you change your clothes and a thin tube is put into a vein
The anesthesiologist gives you pain relief
The surgeon makes a small cut near the belly button, or a few keyhole cuts
What came out through the hernia is put back into the belly
The weak spot is stitched and often strengthened with mesh
The wound is stitched and a dressing is put on
feel: Pain around the wound. You will get pain medicine
In the first days, coughing and getting up hurt. Holding your belly with your hand helps
after: You can usually get up and walk on the same day
Usually no heavy lifting for 4 to 6 weeks. Your surgeon will tell you exactly
Dressing care and showering: follow your doctor's instructions
Wear the support belt, if prescribed
red_flags: Before surgery: the hernia is hard, suddenly painful, will not go back in, or you are vomiting. It may be trapped. Call emergency services
After surgery: a fever above 38 degrees, pain that gets worse, redness or pus at the wound
Vomiting, bloating, or no stools and no gas

faq.q: Can an umbilical hernia go away on its own?
faq.a: In young children it often closes on its own. In adults it does not. Only surgery can fix it.
For a small hernia, stitches alone are sometimes enough. For medium and large ones, a mesh lowers the risk that the hernia comes back. The surgeon decides.

reminders.text: Surgery tomorrow. Pack your things, documents, and list of medicines. Eat and drink only until the time your clinic gave you.
